channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Dushanbe and South Korea Sign Agreement on Smart Transport Development Worth Up to $1.9 Million
item.description: Dushanbe's delegation visited South Korea, resulting in an agreement to develop an intelligent transport system for Tajikistan's capital. The protocol facilitates grant funding from South Korea up to $1.9 million for this project. Discussions also covered intelligent monitoring, traffic management, and public transport efficiency.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Minimum Wage Hike to 110,000 Tenge: Impact on Benefits and Business Costs
item.description: Kazakhstan's minimum wage increase to 110,000 tenge is expected to add approximately 430 billion tenge in salary expenses for businesses. While corporate income tax deductions will decrease, the impact on production costs is anticipated to be minimal. The increase will also raise child care benefits.

item.title: Uzbekistan Updates List of Banned Religious Extremist Sources to 2,057
item.description: Uzbekistan's Supreme Court updated its list of banned religious extremist, terrorist, and radical content to 2,057 items as of November 3. The list includes social media pages, channels, websites, and various materials, with a significant number from Meta platforms and Telegram.

item.title: Otably Bank Relaunches 'Umai' Mortgage Program for Women in Almaty
item.description: Otably Bank has reopened applications for its 'Umai' mortgage program for women in Almaty. The program, which offers loans for new and secondary housing, saw high demand, with 300 applications received by 11:30 AM. The bank is addressing service load issues and processing applications in order.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Revising Moratorium on Private Clinic Inspections
item.description: Kazakhstan is reviewing the moratorium on business inspections, including private clinics. The government is consulting with businesses and state bodies to assess the positive and negative impacts of past moratoria, particularly concerning public health and safety. A decision on potential revisions is expected after analysis.

item.title: KMF Bank Denies Reports of Customer Data Leakage
item.description: KMF Bank has refuted claims of a customer data leak circulating on Telegram channels. A darknet forum user allegedly offered a database for sale, claiming it was extracted from the bank's systems. The bank stated that the information is false and emphasized its commitment to protecting customer data.

item.title: FIFA to Reveal Details of Gianni Infantino's Canceled Secret Plan
item.description: FIFA leadership will review the details of Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in future World Cups to private investors. The $4.2 billion FIFA Forward Enterprise project was halted in July after facing significant global criticism.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank sets 2027 mortgage program funding limit
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank has approved a funding limit of 100 billion tenge for the '7-20-25' mortgage program in 2027, matching the 2026 allocation. Quarterly disbursements will not exceed 25 billion tenge. Funds will be used to purchase mortgage claims from banks, which will issue loans using their own capital.

item.title: Queues form at Otbasy Bank in Almaty as 'Umai' mortgage applications reopen
item.description: A crowd gathered at an Otbasy Bank branch in Almaty on November 3rd as applications for the 'Umai' women's mortgage program reopened. The bank reported receiving 300 applications nationwide by 11:30 AM. Measures are being taken to stabilize services due to high demand. The program is funded by the Asian Development Bank.

item.title: Youth, NGOs, and ethno-cultural groups discuss President's Address in Atyrau
item.description: Representatives of youth, NGOs, and ethno-cultural associations in Atyrau met to discuss the President's Address. The meeting focused on socio-economic development, social protection, national economy, energy, and ecology. Participants received explanations on the Address's priorities and posed questions.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened in Tashkent After Kazakh Footballers Suffer Food Poisoning
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in Tashkent following a food poisoning incident involving young Kazakh footballers participating in the Do'stlik Cup 2026. The Prosecutor General's Office reported that 19 individuals sought medical help, with 17 hospitalized, including 11 children.

item.title: Almaty Discusses Implementation of President's Address from Economic Growth to Rights Protection
item.description: Almaty hosted a discussion on the implementation of the President's address, covering key development areas from economic growth to the protection of citizens' rights. Experts analyzed economic, legal, and social aspects, emphasizing infrastructure modernization and job creation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Government Approves National Action Plan for President's Address
item.description: The Kazakhstan government has approved a draft National Action Plan to implement President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address. The plan includes 96 measures across 12 socio-economic development areas, focusing on national construction, infrastructure, industry support, digital solutions, and entrepreneurship development.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Orders Simplification of Free Medicine Access
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has ordered the simplification of the process for obtaining free medicines. He emphasized the importance of patients receiving full information about available free drugs, locations, and procedures for addressing issues, particularly for those with chronic conditions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allows Businesses to Pay Billions in Taxes in Installments
item.description: Over 1,000 taxpayers in Kazakhstan have utilized tax deferral options since the beginning of the year, totaling 56.4 billion tenge. This includes 873 individual entrepreneurs and 539 legal entities. The Committee of State Revenues stated that the mechanism is primarily used for corporate income tax, social tax, personal income tax, and VAT.

item.title: Kazakhstan and India Sign Extradition Treaty for Wanted Individuals
item.description: Kazakhstan and India have signed an agreement on the extradition of individuals wanted by law enforcement agencies. The treaty was signed by Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General Berik Asylov and India's Ambassador to Kazakhstan, Silas Tangal. This agreement will allow both countries to hand over wanted persons for criminal prosecution or to serve sentences.

item.title: Trump Warns of Potential US Strike on Iran's 'Kuh-e Kalang' Nuclear Facility
item.description: President Donald Trump stated that the United States might target Iran's underground nuclear complex, known as 'Kuh-e Kalang,' if an agreement is not reached. He indicated the strike could occur within an hour if decided. Trump also suggested Iran is eager for a deal and that a good chance of reaching one exists.

item.title: Tajikistan Secures $100 Million Loan for Budget Support
item.description: Tajikistan has received a $100 million loan from the Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development to support its budget. The fund had allocated $200 million in total, with $100 million disbursed to Tajikistan.

item.title: Tashkent Implements "Green Wave" Traffic System on Kokcha Darvoza Street
item.description: Tashkent has launched a "green wave" coordinated traffic light system on Kokcha Darvoza Street, aiming to reduce travel time by an average of 40%. The 7-kilometer stretch now features 16 synchronized traffic lights. The system adjusts to traffic flow, prioritizing green lights for smoother journeys.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Produce 500 More Drug Varieties, Create 1,200 Jobs
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to expand domestic drug production by an additional 500 varieties and create over 1,200 permanent jobs. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that increasing the range of locally produced medications and reducing external supply dependence are strategic goals. The focus is shifting from simple packaging to full-cycle production.

item.title: Uzbekistan Supreme Court Updates List of Banned Sources and Content
item.description: Uzbekistan's Supreme Court has released an updated list of banned sources and content, deeming them imbued with extremist and terrorist ideologies. The list includes 967 items specifically from Telegram channels and groups. This action follows the court's designation of these materials as promoting extremism and terrorism.

item.title: Woman Reunited with Daughter in US After 28 Years, DNA Test Confirms Relation
item.description: Natasha Kalymbetova, who gave up her daughter for adoption due to circumstances in the mid-1990s, has been reunited with her in the US. A DNA test confirmed their biological relationship with 99.999999% certainty. Kalymbetova had previously shared her story of alleged sexual assault and subsequent abandonment of her child.

item.title: International Drug Trafficking Route Disrupted in Caspian Sea, 109 kg Seized
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee reported the disruption of an international drug trafficking route in the Caspian Sea. During a special operation, five individuals were detained, and 109 kilograms of narcotics were confiscated. The seized drugs included opium, hashish, and marijuana. A high-speed boat was also impounded as part of the ongoing investigation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Receive Modern Pacemakers from France for Patients
item.description: Several patients in Kyrgyzstan will receive modern pacemakers from France. A masterclass on leadless cardiac pacing will be held at the National Center of Cardiology and Therapy, attended by the Minister of Health, the French Ambassador, and international experts. A memorandum of understanding between the Kyrgyz Ministry of Health and Paris Public Hospitals is also planned.

item.title: Flash Flood Risk Announced in Nine Regions of Uzbekistan Due to Heavy Rains
item.description: Uzbekistan's hydrometeorological service has warned of potential flash floods and mudflows in foothill and mountainous areas of nine regions from November 4-5 due to anticipated rainfall. Residents in these areas, as well as tourists and drivers, are advised to take precautions. Some areas may experience water accumulation and flooding.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Drug List, Adding New Treatments and Removing Others
item.description: Kazakhstan has expanded its list of outpatient drug provisions by adding 22 modern medications for 14 diseases and removing 52 drugs for 26 conditions. The Ministry of Health reported that 2.1 million patients currently receive free medications for 76 ailments, with electronic prescriptions accounting for 82% of cases. The non-reducible stock of medicines has also been increased by 35%.

item.title: Eldik Bank Unveils Strategic Plans for International Financial Markets
item.description: Eldik Bank's Chairman, Ulanbek Nogaev, discussed the bank's strategic plans in an interview with Bloomberg. Key initiatives include raising up to $500 million through yuan-denominated bonds this year and dollar bonds in 2027. The bank is also preparing for an IPO on the London Stock Exchange, tentatively planned for 2028.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Bukhara to Host UNESCO Creative Cities Network Conference in 2027
item.description: Bukhara, Uzbekistan, will host the 19th annual conference of the UNESCO Creative Cities Network (UCCN) in 2027. The city will be the first in Central Asia, CIS, and the Organization of Turkic States to host this international event. The initiative was proposed by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev.

item.title: Global Chemical Giant to Establish Production Facility in Kazakhstan
item.description: A major global chemical company has decided to commence reagent production within Kazakhstan. The specific reasons behind this strategic decision by the international chemical giant to invest in Kazakhstan are explored in this report.

item.title: Tajikistan and Laos Aim to Expand Investment and Trade Cooperation
item.description: Representatives from Tajikistan's State Committee on Investments discussed strengthening bilateral investment and economic cooperation with Lao counterparts. Key areas included promoting investment opportunities, expanding trade, and fostering industrial, agricultural, and tourism collaboration.

item.title: Kazakhstan Modifies Pension Annuity Rules for Investment Income
item.description: Kazakhstan's financial market regulator has updated rules for calculating pension annuity buy-out sums. New regulations will include investment income in the calculation. Previously, this income might have been paid out separately, potentially reducing future pension payments. The change aims to preserve investment income within the annuity for better future payouts.

item.title: Russian Strike on Kharkiv Hospital Injures 73 People
item.description: A Russian attack on November 3, 2026, damaged a hospital in Kharkiv's Nemyshlyansky district, injuring 73 people, according to Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office. The strike hit a connecting passage between hospital buildings. Authorities reported 62 initial casualties, later updated to 73, including patients, staff, and nearby residents. Over a thousand windows were damaged.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Transfer Vocational Schools to Entrepreneurs for 15 Years
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to transfer two to three vocational schools per region to major entrepreneurs for 15-year management. These institutions are expected to train at least 30,000 specialists annually for domestic and foreign labor markets. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced the initiative, emphasizing the growing demand for skilled workers and the need to align vocational education with employer requirements.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Develop New Ethical Principles for Civil Servants
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to introduce new ethical principles for civil servants, based on the Constitution and principles of service to the state and society. Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin announced the development of a comprehensive plan to strengthen institutional foundations for reforms, with a long-term vision for the country's development.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Discusses Budgets for Aytmatov and Manas Districts
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov met with residents of Aytmatov and Manas districts in Talas region, detailing budget changes and funding for infrastructure projects. Own revenues for Aytmatov district grew from 129 million som in 2021 to 167 million by 2025, with 608 million som allocated for 2026 projects. Manas district saw similar growth.

item.title: Tajikistan produced 18.8 billion kWh of electricity in nine months of 2026
item.description: Tajikistan generated approximately 18.8 billion kWh of electricity from January to September 2026, a 2% decrease compared to the same period in 2025, according to the Statistics Agency. Hydropower plants produced over 17.8 billion kWh, while thermal power plants generated 969 million kWh. Solar power generation increased nearly eightfold, reaching 5.6 million kWh.

item.title: US Lawmakers Urge Administration to Halt Deportation of Afghans
item.description: Sixty-six US lawmakers have urged President Trump's administration to stop the planned deportation of Afghans, citing risks of persecution. A letter sent to the Secretary of State and Homeland Security Secretary highlighted concerns about individuals with links to the former Afghan government and US forces. Advocacy groups noted difficulties in challenging removals due to lack of legal representation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Independently Develop Three Gold Deposits in Talas Region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to independently develop the Taldy-Bulak, Andash, and Bala-Chychkan gold deposits without selling licenses to investors. President Sadyr Japarov stated that a specialist team has been formed within Kyrgyzaltyn for this purpose. The state is already developing Togolok, Kyzyl-Ompol, and Unkur-Tash deposits. Changes to legislation ensure a 30% state share in all deposit development projects.

item.title: France in Talks With Taliban Regarding Return of Irregular Afghan Migrants
item.description: France is in discussions with Taliban officials concerning the return of Afghan migrants residing illegally in the country. The interior minister stated that addressing the return of individuals with irregular status, some of whom may pose a threat to public order, is a priority. Critics accuse the government of normalizing relations with the Taliban.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase LPG Price by 2.5 Times Starting November 15
item.description: Uzbekistan will raise the retail price of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for the population by 2.5 times, from 2000 to 5000 soms per kilogram, effective November 15. Targeted compensation will be provided to low-income families.
